protocol.classification: fixed original winner minus original runner-up logit
protocol.shapley: exact 8 three-modality coalitions, reference feature substitution
protocol.features: 12 conditional straight-line IG edges with Shapley weights; not feature-wise Shapley
protocol.integration: adaptive Gauss-Legendre; marginal completeness AND full-array refinement
protocol.baseline_mean: global TRAIN-only average of observed normalized feature slots, including specials
protocol.baseline_zero: zero in model-input space, not necessarily zero raw acoustic/visual features
protocol.masks: original attention masks held fixed for every intervention
protocol.evidence_slots: content tokens only; padding excluded and specials reported separately
protocol.negative_contribution: reduces fixed classification margin or continuous regression score
protocol.strength_share: absolute modality Shapley divided by sum absolute Shapley
protocol.deletion: ranking by absolute attribution mass; absolute score change and signed changes retained
protocol.caveat: feature-space interventions and UNK word substitutions may be out of distribution; correlated inputs prevent causal interpretation; embedding dimensions lack semantic labels
protocol.scope: five prespecified unlabeled samples, no accuracy/F1/MAE claim; no Whisper or reconstruction

mean_reference.valid_mask: saved attention mask, including CLS/SEP; natural AV zeros retained

figures.name: 01_modality_contributions
figures.question: Which modality changes each prediction, and in which direction?
figures.notes: Five fixed samples, train-mean reference. Shares normalize absolute Shapley values; not accuracy shares. Classification and regression have different units.

figures.name: 02_time_classification
figures.question: Where along the input does the model receive supporting or opposing evidence?
figures.notes: Gray is padding; dotted columns denote CLS/SEP, not ordinary words. Net=sum(features); mass=sum(abs(features)). All valid slots retained, common scale across samples within each column.

figures.name: 03_time_regression
figures.question: Where along the input does the model receive supporting or opposing evidence?
figures.notes: Gray is padding; dotted columns denote CLS/SEP, not ordinary words. Net=sum(features); mass=sum(abs(features)). All valid slots retained, common scale across samples within each column.

figures.name: 04_features_classification
figures.question: Which numerical feature dimensions carry the largest attribution mass?
figures.notes: Top 8 dimensions per modality/sample; zero-based dimension IDs. Aggregated over content slots; special-token contributions are reported separately. Full feature-by-slot arrays are saved; dimensions have no inferred semantic names.

figures.name: 05_features_regression
figures.question: Which numerical feature dimensions carry the largest attribution mass?
figures.notes: Top 8 dimensions per modality/sample; zero-based dimension IDs. Aggregated over content slots; special-token contributions are reported separately. Full feature-by-slot arrays are saved; dimensions have no inferred semantic names.

figures.name: 06_word_interventions
figures.question: Do high-ranked textual representations also matter when their words are perturbed?
figures.notes: Top 5 words per target. Brackets contain original token slots. Whole-sequence re-encoding, audio/video unchanged. Attribution and intervention are different estimands; disagreement is retained, not hidden. No word timestamps inferred.

figures.name: 07_occlusion_validation
figures.question: Does replacing highly attributed evidence change the output more than controls?
figures.notes: Mean-reference replacements at the same aligned slots in all three modalities; fixed masks/targets. Random band is SD over 20 seeded random rankings, not a confidence interval. All outcomes shown; stronger response is not guaranteed. Per-modality controls are in the numerical report.

figures.name: 08_reference_stability
figures.question: Are modality importance and key time slots stable under a different attribution reference?
figures.notes: Top: content-slot Spearman correlation; middle: top-5 Jaccard overlap; bottom: zero-reference minus mean-reference absolute modality share, in percentage points. AV train means in normalized input space are near zero, so this comparison mainly varies the text reference. These are sensitivity diagnostics, not statistical confidence.

reference_stability.limitation: Normalized audio/vision train means are near zero; the alternate reference mainly changes text. Exact ties in top-k ranks use stable original-slot ordering.

reading_guide.01: Modality direction and absolute shares, separately for the two prediction heads.
reading_guide.02-03: Original-slot heatmaps: signed net versus absolute mass. No timestamps.
reading_guide.04-05: Content-slot feature dimension rankings; IDs are numerical, not semantic labels.
reading_guide.06: Whole-word UNK re-encoding: compare interventions with cached-slot attribution.
reading_guide.07: Equal-count occlusion controls: top, low, and seeded random with SD.
reading_guide.08: Reference sensitivity of time-slot rankings, top-5 overlap and modality contribution shares.

explanation_cautions: Absolute Shapley shares are conditional on the reference and fixed masks; they are not causal percentages or accuracy contributions.

The reused model treats zero audio/vision rows at CLS/SEP as valid observations. Its original preprocessing is preserved. Special-slot attributions must not be interpreted as spoken words or real video frames.
Modality Shapley includes special slots; word and feature-dimension rankings exclude them. Net contributions can cancel although attribution mass is large.
Agreement with interventions is sample-specific; inspect all controls, including cases where top-ranked slots do not outperform low or random slots.
No semantic meaning is assigned to embedding dimension IDs; no real-time localization is performed.
